_readme: OWNERSHIP LEDGER for questions the chapterwise compilation files under TWO chapters.
WHY: content_hash dedup is per (org, exam, hash), so an exact duplicate lands in
whichever chapter commits FIRST and the other copy vanishes silently — an arbitrary
outcome that reads like a decision. A near-duplicate (the copies often differ by a
word) lands TWICE instead. Neither is acceptable, so ownership is decided here and
the losing copy is dropped explicitly by `drop` below.
HOW THIS LIST WAS BUILT — worth knowing, because the first attempt was wrong. A
token-similarity threshold of 0.90 found 23 pairs and MISSED at least four genuine
duplicates sitting at 0.76-0.89 (the 'five cards' pair, the 45/60-degree line pair, an
area pair, and the ellipse pair). Cross-chapter filing turns out to concentrate in
exactly four chapter pairs, so the list below comes from reading BOTH sides of those
four pairs in full — 32 pairs. Do not regenerate this by threshold.
SCOPE — cross-chapter ONLY. Same-chapter near-duplicates are deliberately NOT dropped:
they are genuine cross-year repeats (y = x^x set in both 2016 and 2019; the
homogeneous-equation proof in 2016, 2018 and 2020; the same p.d.f. in 2015 and 2017),
and recurrence is signal. See the project rule 'keep duplicates — recurrence signal'.
TWO SEPARATE DECISIONS, deliberately not conflated:
owner   — which chapter the question belongs to, decided on the TEXTBOOK's placement
and the DB subtopic axis, never on which file happened to list it first.
useText — which transcription to keep. The copies are not always identical and the
owner's copy is not always the better one (see the direction-cosine proof).
TAG CAVEAT: the provenance tag is NOT a unique key. 20 tags label different questions,
and eight pairs below disagree with each other on the question NUMBER for the same
question (Q.4(B)v vs Q.5(A)v, March 2015). Year and month agree everywhere; the number
is recorded best-effort and must not be used to reconcile against a raw paper.
NET EFFECT: 352 question instances - 32 dropped = 320 rows to ingest.

pairs._group: Definite Integration -> Application of Definite Integration
pairs._finding: ALL EIGHT of the App-of-Definite-Integration chapter's questions are duplicates of Definite Integration's Q10-Q17 — a perfect 1:1. The compilation cross-filed its whole 'area' block (its own section C, 'Definite Integrals Leading to Area'). So App of Definite Integration contributes ZERO unique questions, and Definite Integration's real contribution is its Q1-Q9 (evaluation + properties).
pairs._rule: AREA questions go to Application of Definite Integration — its two DB subtopics are literally 'Area Under a Curve' and 'Area Between Two Curves'. Definite Integration is about evaluating integrals and proving their properties.

items.defect: RESOLVED 2026-08-13 by reading the page. The two copies gave DIFFERENT ellipses for the same tag — x^2/1 + y^2/4 = 1 (Definite Integration) vs x^2/1 + y^2/9 = 1 (App of Definite Integration) — and arithmetic could not choose between them, both being well-formed ellipses with clean areas (2pi and 3pi). Maths 2018 paper.pdf page index 2, rendered at 120 dpi over 0.61-0.92 of page height, prints 'Find the area of ellipse x^2/1 + y^2/4 = 1.' — so the Definite Integration copy is faithful and the App-of-Definite-Integration copy is the transcription error. This is exactly what the keep/useText split exists for: the question belongs to Application of Definite Integration by its subtopic axis, but its correct TEXT is in the copy being dropped. Area = pi*a*b = 2pi.

items.note: Copies disagree on the question number (iii. vs iv.).

items.defect: RESOLVED 2026-08-13 — the MCQ had ZERO options in BOTH copies; the four printed options were recovered from Maths 2025 paper.pdf and are in defects.json (mcqOptionsLost.recovered). Its (a) 2/17 and (c) 17/2 were read at 300 dpi precisely because flattened text would have made them look like a duplicate-option defect; they are genuinely different stacked fractions. Answer 17/2.

pairs._finding: Five pairs, all direction-cosine / direction-ratio questions.
pairs._rule: Direction cosines and ratios are taught in the VECTORS chapter, not Line and Planes — verified in the textbook AGAINST the opposite assumption. Ch.5 carries 38 'direction cosine' mentions and a dedicated section 5.3.4 'Direction Angles and Direction Cosines' sitting inside 5.3 Product of vectors (→ DB subtopic 'Dot Product of Vectors'); Ch.6's section list opens at 6.1 'Vector and Cartesian equations of a line' and has no DC/DR section at all. The shipped bank already files 15 DC/DR practice rows under Vectors → Dot Product.
pairs._notADuplicate: Vectors#23 [Q. 18, March 2023] and Line-and-Plane#1 [Q. 1.(B) i., March 2015] share the SAME direction ratios (-2,1,-1 and -3,-4,1) but ask for different things (ratios vs cosines) in different sittings. Two distinct PYQs that reuse data — both kept.

items.why: The Vectors copy's math zone is truncated — it reads 'then $= $ ____' with the quantity lost. The Line-and-Plane copy has 'then r = ____' intact.

The dropped copy is the better text and must be carried over: it is FULLER (keeps the second part, 'Hence find the direction angles of the line with the X axis') and more correct — the Vectors copy writes the direction cosines as l-hat, m-hat, n-hat, putting unit-vector hats on scalars.
Direction ratios of a vector perpendicular to two lines is solved by the cross product, so this one sits on Cross Product rather than Dot Product. The bank already files 2 DC/DR practice rows there.
Line makes 45 and 60 degrees with the Y and Z axes; find the angle with X. Missed by the 0.90 threshold at 0.83.

pairs._rule: Monotonicity, extrema and the mean value theorems are APPLICATIONS of the derivative and each has its own subtopic on Application of Derivatives. Differentiation's eight subtopics are all differentiation METHODS and offer no home for them.

items.why: Keep the owner's copy — it bolds the theorem name, matching how the shipped practice rows on that subtopic are written.

pairs._finding: FIFTEEN of Binomial Distribution's SIXTEEN questions duplicate Probability Distributions. Only its Q5 [Q. 33, February 2020] (fair coin tossed 8 times) is unique to it. So the two chapters are largely one corpus filed twice.
pairs._rule: A question whose model is explicitly X~B(n,p), or which is a count of successes over n repeated independent trials (n tosses / n bombs / n patients / n cards with replacement), is BINOMIAL. A general p.m.f./p.d.f., or an expectation computed from a bare distribution table, stays in Probability Distributions.
pairs._blocked: NEITHER chapter exists in the DB yet — both are created by Phase 1 (the textbook ingest of Ch_07 and Ch_08). Adjudicated on content here, but not committable until then, and the `subtopic` fields are deliberately absent because that axis does not exist yet.
_notADuplicate: Probability#2 [Q. 6.(A) ii., March 2015] uses the same 4Cx (5/9)^x (4/9)^(4-x) p.m.f. as Probability#15 / Binomial#12 [Q. 1. viii., March 2023], but it is a different sitting asking a different thing — cross-year recurrence, both kept.
Probability#3 [March 2015] and Probability#6 [March 2017] are the same p.d.f. question in two sittings — same-chapter recurrence, both kept.
